newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - ING lifts Q1 profit 21 pct,stays cautious.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - ING lifts Q1 profit 21 pct,stays cautious.

text.p: Dutch financial services giant ING Groep on Thursday underlined its conservative image when it announced a 21 percent hike in first quarter profits but declined to make a forecast of its full year prospects.
Although the result met market expectations and would have surpassed them if not for further provisions for future expenses, shares in the group slipped on profit taking.
Net profit in the first three months of 1997 grew to 891 million guilders ($465.4 million) from 736 million a year earlier, continuing the momentum of 1996 when earnings rose 25.4 percent.
"After the excellent results for 1996, the result for the first three months of 1997 showed continued strong growth," ING said.
As in 1996, the internationally spread group's banking operations were the main profit driver, increasing earnings by 26.5 percent against a 14.6 percent rise by the insurance activities.
ING said business volumes rose considerably, with life premium income growing 26 percent, non-life premiums 12 percent and banking income 23 percent.
It identified the Netherlands, North America and Australia as sources of strong profit growth from life and non-life insurance.
Fire insurance operations returned to profit due to fewer weather-related claims, but motor profits declined mainly as a result of the severe winter in Canada.
The group said strong growth in the volume of loans outweighed a narrowing of interest margins to produce a 17.9 percent increase in net interest income.

It said bullish financial markets contributed to the 40.2 percent boost in trading income and an increase in assets under managment, while ING Barings and Baring Asset Management (MAM) figured prominently as commission income surged 36.8 percent.
MAM and part of ING Barings were formerly owned by Barings, the British merchant bank which ING rescued in 1995 after Barings almost collapsed from derivatives losses.
Currency exchange rate movements added 41 million guilders to the result.
ING also set aside another 200 million guilders for future expenses such as the introduction of the euro single currency, the millennium, restructuring and information technology.
This charge, most of which relates to banking, is in addition to 530 million set aside for future expenses in 1996.

ING said results in the first quarter were favourable, but it declined to give a profit forecast for the full year because it has launched a share offering to coincide with its planned share listing on the New York Stock Exchange on June 13.
Analysts said the results, in line with expectations ranging between 850 million and 946 million guilders, were even better than they looked because of the extra provisions.
"These figures are very nice. Earnings per share were exactly as we had expected, and the quality of the results is very good," said Bart van der Feen of IRIS Research.
BZW analyst Heinie Hakker said the Dutch group had set aside more provisions for future expenses than originally indicated but it had declined to provide more details about them.
"They're so conservative. I find it a bit strange when you put aside so much money but refuse to show what it's for."
The group's shares weakened on the results, trading at 87.00 guilders at 1320 GMT, down 1.20 on the day and 2.00 guilders below the level reached just before the announcement.
"I think there's some profit taking going on," Hakker added.
($ = 1.914 Dutch Guilders)
